source.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מֵעֵ֖בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And set out [the] sons of Israel and camped in [the] plains of Moab, beyond [the] Jordan [at] Jericho.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan [from] Jericho.
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved on and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved on. They set up camp on the flat land of Moab, across the Jordan River from the city of Jericho.

es.L: Y partieron los hijos de Israel y acamparon en las llanuras de Moab, al otro lado del Jordán, [frente a] Jericó.
es.B: Luego los israelitas siguieron su camino y acamparon en las llanuras de Moab, al otro lado del Jordán, frente a Jericó.
es.R: Después los israelitas siguieron adelante. Pusieron su campamento en la llanura de Moab, al otro lado del río Jordán, frente a la ciudad de Jericó.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël partirent et campèrent dans les plaines de Moab, au-delà du Jourdain, [en face de] Jéricho.
fr.B: Puis les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} levèrent le camp et s’installèrent dans les plaines de Moab, de l’autre côté du Jourdain, en face de Jéricho.
fr.R: Ensuite, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont repartis. Ils ont installé leur camp dans la plaine de Moab, de l’autre côté du fleuve Jourdain, en face de la ville de Jéricho.

sw.L: Kisha wana wa Israeli wakasafiri, wakapiga kambi katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, ng'ambo ya Yordani [mkabala na] Yeriko.
sw.B: Kisha Waisraeli waliondoka, wakapiga kambi katika nchi tambarare za Moabu, ng'ambo ya Yordani, mkabala na Yeriko.
sw.R: Baadaye Waisraeli waliondoka tena. Walipiga kambi katika nchi tambarare ya Moabu, ng'ambo ya Mto Yordani, mkabala na mji wa Yeriko.

decisions.choice: the plains of Moab: the low land east of the Jordan, just north of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: This is Israel's last camp before they cross into Canaan. They are still here at the end of the book (33:48-50; 36:13), and Moses dies on a mountain above it (Deuteronomy 34:1, 8). The land had belonged to Moab before Sihon the Amorite took it from them (21:26).

decisions.choice: across the Jordan from Jericho: on the east bank, facing Jericho on the west
decisions.reason: "Beyond the Jordan" is said from the point of view of the land west of the river, the land Israel is about to enter. Jericho lies on the other side of the river from the camp; it is the first town Israel will take (Joshua 6).

decisions.choice: the flat land of Moab, the Jordan River, the city of Jericho
decisions.reason: Readable explains "plains" and says what the Jordan and Jericho are, for readers who do not know the places.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("partirent", "campèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("sont repartis", "ont installé")
decisions.reason: The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as spoken and school French does (docs/french-style.md section 3).

source.text: וַיַּ֥רְא בָּלָ֖ק בֶּן־צִפּ֑וֹר אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לָֽאֱמֹרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Balak son of Zippor all that had done Israel to the Amorite[s].

en.L: And Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
en.B: Balak son of Zippor saw everything that Israel had done to the Amorites.
en.R: Balak son of Zippor had seen all that Israel had done to the Amorites.

es.L: Y vio Balac hijo de Zipor todo lo que Israel había hecho a los amorreos.
es.B: Balac hijo de Zipor vio todo lo que Israel había hecho a los amorreos.
es.R: Balac, hijo de Zipor, había visto todo lo que Israel les había hecho a los amorreos.

fr.L: Et Balak fils de Tsippor vit tout ce qu’Israël avait fait aux Amoréens.
fr.B: Balak, fils de Tsippor, vit tout ce qu’Israël avait fait aux Amoréens.
fr.R: Balak, le fils de Tsippor, avait vu tout ce qu’Israël avait fait aux Amoréens.

sw.L: Naye Balaki mwana wa Sipori akaona yote ambayo Israeli alikuwa amewatendea Waamori.
sw.B: Balaki mwana wa Sipori aliona yote ambayo Israeli aliwatendea Waamori.
sw.R: Balaki mwana wa Sipori alikuwa ameona mambo yote ambayo Waisraeli waliwafanyia Waamori.

decisions.choice: all that Israel had done to the Amorites: the defeat of Sihon and Og
decisions.reason: Israel had just defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and taken his towns, and then Og king of Bashan (21:21-35). Both are called "the two kings of the Amorites" (Deuteronomy 3:8). Their lands lay on Moab's northern border, so Balak had watched it happen close by.

decisions.choice: Balak son of Zippor: a king of Moab known from this story
decisions.reason: The narrator names Balak first and says only in verse 4 that he was king of Moab. Later Scripture remembers him for hiring Balaam against Israel (Joshua 24:9; Judges 11:25; Micah 6:5).

source.text: וַיָּ֨גָר מוֹאָ֜ב מִפְּנֵ֥י הָעָ֛ם מְאֹ֖ד כִּ֣י רַב־ה֑וּא וַיָּ֣קָץ מוֹאָ֔ב מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And was afraid Moab from before the people exceedingly, for numerous [was] it; and felt dread Moab before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And Moab was greatly afraid of the people, for it [was] numerous; and Moab felt dread before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many of them; Moab felt a sickening dread of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: The people of Moab were terrified, because the Israelites were so many. They felt sick with fear of them.

es.L: Y Moab tuvo gran temor del pueblo, porque [era] numeroso; y Moab sintió pavor ante los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Moab estaba aterrado ante aquel pueblo, porque eran muchísimos; Moab sentía ante los israelitas un miedo que lo enfermaba.
es.R: Los habitantes de Moab estaban aterrados, porque los israelitas eran muchísimos. Les tenían tanto miedo que se sentían enfermos.

fr.L: Et Moab eut très peur du peuple, car il [était] nombreux ; et Moab fut saisi d’effroi devant les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël.
fr.B: Moab fut terrifié par ce peuple, parce qu’ils étaient si nombreux ; Moab était malade de peur devant les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.
fr.R: Les habitants de Moab étaient terrifiés, parce que les Israélites étaient si nombreux. Ils en étaient malades de peur.

sw.L: Naye Moabu akaogopa sana mbele ya watu hao, kwa sababu [walikuwa] wengi; naye Moabu akaingiwa na hofu kuu mbele ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Moabu aliwaogopa sana watu hao kwa kuwa walikuwa wengi mno; Moabu akajawa na hofu iliyomtia kichefuchefu mbele ya Waisraeli.
sw.R: Watu wa Moabu waliogopa sana, kwa sababu Waisraeli walikuwa wengi mno. Waliwaogopa kiasi cha kujisikia wagonjwa.

decisions.choice: felt dread: a sickened fear, close to loathing
decisions.reason: The second verb is stronger than the first. It is the word used of the Egyptians, who "dreaded" the Israelites as their numbers grew (Exodus 1:12). Moab now feels what Egypt felt, and for the same reason: there are so many of them.

decisions.choice: Moab: the nation, spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular: Moab the nation is afraid, as one body, as "Israel" is in verse 2.

decisions.choice: The people of Moab
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Moab" so that the reader does not take Moab for a single man.

decisions.choice: "hofu iliyomtia kichefuchefu" (a fear that made him sick)
decisions.reason: The second verb is a sickened dread, close to loathing (see m1); Balanced keeps the sense of nausea, as the English "sickening dread" does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מוֹאָ֜ב אֶל־זִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן עַתָּ֞ה יְלַחֲכ֤וּ הַקָּהָל֙ אֶת־כָּל־סְבִ֣יבֹתֵ֔ינוּ כִּלְחֹ֣ךְ הַשּׁ֔וֹר אֵ֖ת יֶ֣רֶק הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּבָלָ֧ק בֶּן־צִפּ֛וֹר מֶ֥לֶךְ לְמוֹאָ֖ב בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moab to [the] elders of Midian, now will lick up the assembly all around us, as licks up the ox [the] green of the field. And Balak son of Zippor [was] king of Moab at the time, that [one].

en.L: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, "Now the assembly will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the green growth of the field." And Balak son of Zippor [was] king of Moab at that time.
en.B: So Moab said to the elders of Midian, "Now this assembly will lick up everything around us, as an ox crops the grass of a field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.
en.R: The Moabites said to the elders of Midian, "This crowd will soon eat up everything around us, as an ox eats up the grass in a field." At that time Balak son of Zippor was the king of Moab.

es.L: Y dijo Moab a los ancianos de Madián: «Ahora lamerá la asamblea todo lo que está alrededor de nosotros, como lame el buey la hierba verde del campo». Y Balac hijo de Zipor [era] rey de Moab en aquel tiempo.
es.B: Así que Moab dijo a los ancianos de Madián: «Ahora esta asamblea va a lamer todo lo que nos rodea, como el buey arranca la hierba del campo». Balac hijo de Zipor era rey de Moab en aquel tiempo.
es.R: Los moabitas dijeron a los ancianos de Madián: «Esta multitud pronto se va a comer todo lo que hay a nuestro alrededor, como un buey se come la hierba de un campo». En ese tiempo, Balac hijo de Zipor era el rey de Moab.

fr.L: Et Moab dit aux anciens de Madian : « Maintenant, l’assemblée va lécher tout ce qui est autour de nous, comme le bœuf lèche la verdure des champs. » Et Balak fils de Tsippor [était] roi de Moab en ce temps-là.
fr.B: Moab dit donc aux anciens de Madian : « Maintenant cette assemblée va tout lécher autour de nous, comme un bœuf broute l’herbe d’un champ. » Balak, fils de Tsippor, était roi de Moab à cette époque.
fr.R: Les Moabites ont dit aux anciens de Madian : « Cette foule va bientôt tout dévorer autour de nous, comme un bœuf mange l’herbe d’un champ. » À cette époque, Balak, fils de Tsippor, était le roi de Moab.

sw.L: Naye Moabu akawaambia wazee wa Midiani, "Sasa kusanyiko hili litaramba vyote vilivyo kandokando yetu, kama ng'ombe arambavyo majani mabichi ya shambani." Naye Balaki mwana wa Sipori [alikuwa] mfalme wa Moabu wakati huo.
sw.B: Basi Moabu akawaambia wazee wa Midiani, "Sasa kusanyiko hili litaramba kila kitu kinachotuzunguka, kama ng'ombe anavyokula majani ya shambani." Balaki mwana wa Sipori ndiye aliyekuwa mfalme wa Moabu wakati huo.
sw.R: Wamoabu waliwaambia wazee wa Midiani, "Umati huu utakula upesi kila kitu kinachotuzunguka, kama ng'ombe anavyokula nyasi shambani." Wakati huo Balaki mwana wa Sipori ndiye aliyekuwa mfalme wa Moabu.

decisions.choice: the elders of Midian: the leaders of a people allied with Moab
decisions.reason: Midian was a people of tribes and clans, led by elders and chiefs (31:8). Moses' wife was a Midianite (Exodus 2:16-21). Here Midian joins Moab against Israel; Midianite women take part in leading Israel astray in chapter 25, and Israel's war against Midian in chapter 31 ends with Balaam's death (31:8, 16).

decisions.choice: lick up as the ox licks up the grass: use up the land completely
decisions.reason: An ox grazing strips a field bare. Moab fears that Israel will consume everything around it, as it had just taken the land of the Amorites (21:24-25). The picture comes from a people of herdsmen.

decisions.choice: Balak ... was king of Moab at that time: background given in passing
decisions.reason: The narrator pauses to say who Balak is before he acts in verse 5.

decisions.choice: assembly (L, B), crowd (R)
decisions.reason: The word usually names Israel gathered as a people (as in 20:4). Here Moab uses it for Israel as a great mass of people, so Readable says "crowd".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכִ֜ים אֶל־בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־בְּע֗וֹר פְּ֠תוֹרָה אֲשֶׁ֧ר עַל־הַנָּהָ֛ר אֶ֥רֶץ בְּנֵי־עַמּ֖וֹ לִקְרֹא־ל֑וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִ֠נֵּה עַ֣ם יָצָ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ הִנֵּ֤ה כִסָּה֙ אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְה֥וּא יֹשֵׁ֖ב מִמֻּלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, to Pethor, which [is] by the River, [the] land of [the] sons of his people, to call him, saying, look, a people has come out from Egypt; look, it has covered the eye of the land, and it [is] dwelling opposite me.

en.L: And he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which [is] by the River, [in the] land of the {{gender:children|sons}} of his people, to call him, saying, "Look, a people has come out of Egypt. Look, it has covered the eye of the land, and it is dwelling opposite me.
en.B: He sent messengers to call Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, near the River, in the land of his own people. The message said, "A people has come out of Egypt. They are covering the face of the land, and they have settled right across from me.
en.R: So Balak sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor. Balaam lived in the town of Pethor, near the Euphrates River, in the land of his own people. Balak wanted Balaam to come to him. His message said, "A whole nation has come out of Egypt. They cover the land, and they are living right next to me.

es.L: Y envió mensajeros a Balaam hijo de Beor, a Petor, que [está] junto al Río, [en la] tierra de los hijos de su pueblo, para llamarlo, diciendo: «Mira, un pueblo ha salido de Egipto; mira, ha cubierto el ojo de la tierra, y habita frente a mí.
es.B: Envió mensajeros a llamar a Balaam hijo de Beor, en Petor, cerca del Río, en la tierra de su propio pueblo. El mensaje decía: «Ha salido de Egipto un pueblo. Está cubriendo la faz de la tierra, y se ha establecido justo enfrente de mí.
es.R: Entonces Balac envió mensajeros a Balaam hijo de Beor. Balaam vivía en la ciudad de Petor, cerca del río Éufrates, en la tierra de su propio pueblo. Balac quería que Balaam fuera a verlo. Su mensaje decía: «Toda una nación ha salido de Egipto. Cubren la tierra, y viven justo a mi lado.

fr.L: Et il envoya des messagers à Balaam fils de Béor, à Pethor, qui [est] près du Fleuve, [dans le] pays des {{gender:enfants|fils}} de son peuple, pour l’appeler, en disant : « Voici, un peuple est sorti d’Égypte ; voici, il a couvert l’œil du pays, et il habite en face de moi.
fr.B: Il envoya des messagers appeler Balaam, fils de Béor, à Pethor, près du Fleuve, dans le pays de son propre peuple. Le message disait : « Un peuple est sorti d’Égypte. Il recouvre la surface du pays, et il s’est établi juste en face de moi.
fr.R: Alors Balak a envoyé des messagers chez Balaam, fils de Béor. Balaam habitait la ville de Pethor, près du fleuve Euphrate, dans le pays de son propre peuple. Balak voulait que Balaam vienne le voir. Son message disait : « Tout un peuple est sorti d’Égypte. Ils couvrent le pays, et ils habitent juste à côté de chez moi.

sw.L: Naye akatuma wajumbe kwa Balaamu mwana wa Beori, huko Pethori, iliyo karibu na Mto, [katika] nchi ya wana wa watu wake, ili kumwita, akisema, "Tazama, watu wametoka Misri; tazama, wamefunika jicho la nchi, nao wanakaa mkabala nami.
sw.B: Alituma wajumbe kumwita Balaamu mwana wa Beori, huko Pethori karibu na Mto, katika nchi ya watu wake mwenyewe. Ujumbe ulisema, "Watu fulani wametoka Misri. Wameenea juu ya uso wa nchi, nao wamekaa mkabala nami kabisa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Balaki alituma wajumbe kwa Balaamu mwana wa Beori. Balaamu aliishi katika mji wa Pethori, karibu na Mto Frati, katika nchi ya watu wake mwenyewe. Balaki alitaka Balaamu aje kwake. Ujumbe wake ulisema, "Taifa zima limetoka Misri. Wameijaza nchi, nao wanaishi karibu kabisa nami.

decisions.choice: Balaam son of Beor: a famous seer from far away
decisions.reason: Balaam is a man people sent for to bless or to curse (verse 6). Later Scripture remembers him as a diviner (Joshua 13:22) who was hired against Israel (Deuteronomy 23:5; Nehemiah 13:2). A wall inscription found at Deir Alla in Jordan, written some centuries later, speaks of "Balaam son of Beor" as a seer of the gods, so his name was known outside Israel too.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" with no other name usually means the Euphrates (Genesis 31:21; Exodus 23:31). Deuteronomy 23:5 places Pethor in Aram-naharaim, "Aram of the two rivers", in upper Mesopotamia, and Balaam says he came "from Aram" (23:7). It was a journey of many days from Moab.

decisions.choice: the land of the sons of his people: Balaam's homeland
alternatives: the land of the sons of Ammon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "his people" ('ammo). The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Syriac and the Latin Vulgate read "Ammon", a very similar word, which would put Balaam close to Moab. The Hebrew reading fits "the River" and Aram (23:7) and is kept. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: covered the eye of the land: spread over the land like a swarm
decisions.reason: The same words describe the locusts that covered Egypt (Exodus 10:5, 15). Balak pictures Israel as a swarm that leaves nothing behind (compare verse 4).

decisions.choice: the town of Pethor, the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Readable names the river the Hebrew calls simply "the River" (see m2) and splits the long sentence.

decisions.choice: the eye of the land
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, as in Exodus 10:5; Balanced says "the face of the land".

decisions.choice: "le Fleuve" with a capital
decisions.reason: "The River" with no other name is the Euphrates (see m2); the capital marks it as a name, as the English "the River" does. Readable names the Euphrates.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֩ לְכָה־נָּ֨א אָֽרָה־לִּ֜י אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה כִּֽי־עָצ֥וּם הוּא֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי אוּלַ֤י אוּכַל֙ נַכֶּה־בּ֔וֹ וַאֲגָרְשֶׁ֖נּוּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־תְּבָרֵךְ֙ מְבֹרָ֔ךְ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּאֹ֖ר יוּאָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And now come, please, curse for me the people this, for mighty [is] it more than I; perhaps I will be able [that] we strike it and I drive it out from the land; for I know that whom you bless [is] blessed, and whom you curse is cursed.

en.L: And now come, please, curse this people for me, for it [is] too mighty for me. Perhaps I will be able [so that] we may strike it, and I may drive it out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless [is] blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
en.B: So come now, please, and curse this people for me, because they are too strong for me. Perhaps then we will be able to defeat them, and I can drive them out of the land. For I know this: those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed."
en.R: Please come and curse these people for me. They are too strong for me. If you curse them, perhaps we will be able to defeat them, and I can drive them out of the land. I know that when you bless people, they are blessed. And when you curse people, they are cursed."

es.L: Y ahora ven, te ruego, maldíceme este pueblo, porque [es] demasiado poderoso para mí. Quizá podré [hacer que] lo derrotemos y lo echaré de la tierra; porque yo sé que el que tú bendices [es] bendito, y el que tú maldices es maldito».
es.B: Ven, pues, te lo ruego, y maldice a este pueblo por mí, porque son más fuertes que yo. Quizá así podamos vencerlos y yo pueda expulsarlos de la tierra. Porque sé esto: aquellos a quienes bendices quedan benditos, y aquellos a quienes maldices quedan malditos».
es.R: Por favor, ven y maldice a este pueblo por mí. Son demasiado fuertes para mí. Si tú los maldices, tal vez podamos vencerlos, y yo pueda echarlos de la tierra. Yo sé que cuando tú bendices a alguien, queda bendecido. Y cuando maldices a alguien, queda maldito».

fr.L: Et maintenant, viens, je te prie, maudis-moi ce peuple, car il [est] trop puissant pour moi. Peut-être pourrai-je [faire en sorte que] nous le frappions, et je le chasserai du pays ; car je sais que celui que tu bénis [est] béni, et celui que tu maudis est maudit. »
fr.B: Viens donc, je t’en prie, et maudis ce peuple pour moi, car il est trop fort pour moi. Peut-être alors pourrons-nous le battre, et je pourrai le chasser du pays. Car je le sais : ceux que tu bénis sont bénis, et ceux que tu maudis sont maudits. »
fr.R: S’il te plaît, viens maudire ce peuple pour moi. Ils sont trop forts pour moi. Si tu les maudis, nous pourrons peut-être les battre, et je pourrai les chasser du pays. Je sais que les gens que tu bénis sont bénis, et que les gens que tu maudis sont maudits. »

sw.L: Basi sasa njoo, tafadhali, unilaanie watu hawa, kwa kuwa [wana] nguvu kuliko mimi. Huenda nitaweza [kufanya] tuwapige, nami niwafukuze kutoka katika nchi; kwa maana najua kwamba yule umbarikiye [amebarikiwa], na yule umlaaniye amelaaniwa."
sw.B: Basi njoo sasa, tafadhali, unilaanie watu hawa, kwa sababu wana nguvu kuliko mimi. Huenda hapo tutaweza kuwashinda, nami nitaweza kuwafukuza kutoka katika nchi. Kwa maana najua jambo hili: wale unaowabariki hubarikiwa, na wale unaowalaani hulaaniwa."
sw.R: Tafadhali, njoo uwalaani watu hawa kwa ajili yangu. Wana nguvu kuliko mimi. Ukiwalaani, huenda tutaweza kuwashinda, nami nitaweza kuwafukuza kutoka nchi hii. Ninajua kwamba ukiwabariki watu, wanabarikiwa. Na ukiwalaani watu, wanalaaniwa."

decisions.choice: curse: call down ruin by solemn words
decisions.reason: To curse was to speak words meant to bring harm on someone by calling on divine power. Balak wants Israel weakened before he fights them.

decisions.choice: perhaps I will be able, we may strike it: Balak with his army
decisions.reason: Balak speaks of himself ("I will be able", "I may drive it out"), but the verb for striking is "we". He means himself and his fighting men together. The mixed forms are kept.

decisions.choice: whoever you bless is blessed: Balak thinks the power lies in the seer's words
decisions.reason: Balak treats blessing and cursing as a power Balaam can sell. The story answers him: Balaam can say only what God puts in his mouth (verses 18, 38), and God had already said that those who bless Abraham's family will be blessed and those who curse it will be cursed (Genesis 12:3; Numbers 24:9).

decisions.choice: If you curse them
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Balak's hope of winning rests on the curse, as the order of his words implies.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ זִקְנֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּקְסָמִ֖ים בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו דִּבְרֵ֥י בָלָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] elders of Moab and [the] elders of Midian, and divinations [were] in their hand; and they came to Balaam and spoke to him [the] words of Balak.

en.L: And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, with [the fees for] divination in their hand; and they came to Balaam and spoke to him the words of Balak.
en.B: So the elders of Moab and of Midian set out, carrying the payment for divination. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak's message.
en.R: The elders of Moab and Midian left, taking money with them to pay Balaam for reading omens. They came to Balaam and told him what Balak had said.

es.L: Y fueron los ancianos de Moab y los ancianos de Madián, con [la paga de la] adivinación en su mano; y llegaron a Balaam y le dijeron las palabras de Balac.
es.B: Los ancianos de Moab y de Madián partieron, pues, llevando el pago por la adivinación. Llegaron a donde estaba Balaam y le dieron el mensaje de Balac.
es.R: Los ancianos de Moab y de Madián se fueron, y llevaron dinero para pagarle a Balaam por leer los presagios. Llegaron adonde estaba Balaam y le contaron lo que Balac había dicho.

fr.L: Et les anciens de Moab et les anciens de Madian allèrent, avec [le prix de la] divination dans leur main ; et ils vinrent vers Balaam et lui dirent les paroles de Balak.
fr.B: Les anciens de Moab et de Madian partirent donc, emportant de quoi payer la divination. Ils arrivèrent chez Balaam et lui transmirent le message de Balak.
fr.R: Les anciens de Moab et de Madian sont partis. Ils ont emporté de l’argent pour payer Balaam, pour qu’il lise les présages. Ils sont arrivés chez Balaam et lui ont répété ce que Balak avait dit.

sw.L: Basi wazee wa Moabu na wazee wa Midiani wakaenda, wakiwa na [malipo ya] uaguzi mkononi mwao; wakafika kwa Balaamu, wakamwambia maneno ya Balaki.
sw.B: Basi wazee wa Moabu na wa Midiani waliondoka, wakichukua malipo ya uaguzi. Wakafika kwa Balaamu, wakampa ujumbe wa Balaki.
sw.R: Wazee wa Moabu na wa Midiani waliondoka. Walichukua pesa za kumlipa Balaamu ili aangalie ishara na kuagua. Walifika kwa Balaamu, wakamweleza yale ambayo Balaki alisema.

decisions.choice: divinations in their hand: the fee for divination
decisions.reason: The word means divination, reading signs to learn what is hidden or what is coming. Carried "in their hand", it must mean the payment for it, as a gift was brought to a seer (1 Samuel 9:7-8). Israel's law forbids divination (Deuteronomy 18:10), and Joshua 13:22 calls Balaam "the diviner".

decisions.choice: the elders of Moab and of Midian: both peoples send envoys
decisions.reason: The two peoples act together, as in verse 4. From verse 8 on, the envoys are called Balak's "princes".

decisions.choice: [the fees for] divination
decisions.reason: Literal adds in brackets what the plain word means here (see m1).

decisions.choice: "uaguzi", "kuagua" (divination, reading signs)
decisions.reason: "Uchawi" is witchcraft, harmful magic, which is not what the word means; "uaguzi" is reading signs to learn what is hidden, the sense here (see m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לִ֤ינוּ פֹה֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי־מוֹאָ֖ב עִם־בִּלְעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, lodge here the night, and I will bring back to you word as speaks YHWH to me. And stayed [the] princes of Moab with Balaam.

en.L: And he said to them, "Lodge here tonight, and I will bring you back word, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} speaks to me." And the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
en.B: Balaam told them, "Stay here tonight. I will bring you a reply, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tells it to me." So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
en.R: Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight. Then I will tell you what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to me." So the leaders from Moab stayed with Balaam.

es.L: Y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} aquí la noche, y {{plural_you:les|os}} traeré respuesta, según me hable {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}». Y se quedaron los príncipes de Moab con Balaam.
es.B: Balaam les dijo: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí esta noche. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} traeré la respuesta tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me la dé». Así que los dignatarios de Moab se quedaron con Balaam.
es.R: Balaam les dijo: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí esta noche. Después {{plural_you:les|os}} diré lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me diga». Entonces los jefes de Moab se quedaron con Balaam.

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Passez ici la nuit, et je vous rapporterai une parole, selon ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dira. » Et les princes de Moab demeurèrent chez Balaam.
fr.B: Balaam leur dit : « Restez ici cette nuit. Je vous rapporterai la réponse, telle que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me la donnera. » Les dignitaires de Moab restèrent donc chez Balaam.
fr.R: Balaam leur a dit : « Restez ici cette nuit. Ensuite je vous dirai ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’aura dit. » Alors les chefs de Moab sont restés chez Balaam.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Laleni hapa usiku huu, nami nitawaletea neno, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyoniambia." Nao wakuu wa Moabu wakakaa kwa Balaamu.
sw.B: Balaamu aliwaambia, "Kaeni hapa usiku huu. Nitawaletea jibu, kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyoniambia." Basi maafisa wa Moabu wakakaa kwa Balaamu.
sw.R: Balaamu aliwaambia, "Kaeni hapa usiku huu. Kisha nitawaambia yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataniambia." Kwa hiyo viongozi wa Moabu walikaa kwa Balaamu.

decisions.choice: as the LORD speaks to me: a foreign seer names Israel's God
decisions.reason: Balaam uses the divine name, YHWH. He claims to receive words from Israel's God, and the story shows the LORD really speaking to him, while it also shows that Balaam cannot make God serve his own ends (verses 12, 20, 22).

decisions.choice: lodge here tonight: waiting for word given at night
decisions.reason: God comes to Balaam at night (verses 9, 20), as he speaks to others in dreams by night (Genesis 20:3; 31:24). Balaam expects an answer by morning.

decisions.choice: princes: the king's high officials
decisions.reason: The word names men of rank who serve a king. These are the elders of verse 7, now seen as Balak's envoys.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "princes"; Balanced says "officials", since they are not the king's sons, and Readable says "leaders". The same words are used through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "los dignatarios" for the English Balanced "officials"
decisions.reason: "Funcionarios" sounds like a modern civil service; "dignatarios" names men of rank sent by a king. Literal keeps "príncipes", Readable says "jefes", through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "les dignitaires" for the English Balanced "officials"
decisions.reason: French "officiers" now suggests the army and "fonctionnaires" the civil service; "dignitaires" names men of rank at a king's court. Literal keeps "princes", Readable says "chefs", through the chapter.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֛י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came God to Balaam and said, who [are] the men these with you?

en.L: And God came to Balaam and said, "Who [are] these men with you?"
en.B: God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men staying with you?"
en.R: That night God came to Balaam. He asked him, "Who are these men who are with you?"

es.L: Y vino Dios a Balaam y dijo: «¿Quiénes [son] estos hombres contigo?».
es.B: Dios vino a Balaam y le preguntó: «¿Quiénes son estos hombres que se hospedan contigo?».
es.R: Esa noche, Dios vino a Balaam. Le preguntó: «¿Quiénes son estos hombres que están contigo?».

fr.L: Et Dieu vint vers Balaam et dit : « Qui [sont] ces hommes avec toi ? »
fr.B: Dieu vint à Balaam et lui demanda : « Qui sont ces hommes qui logent chez toi ? »
fr.R: Pendant la nuit, Dieu est venu voir Balaam. Il lui a demandé : « Qui sont ces hommes qui sont avec toi ? »

sw.L: Naye Mungu akamjia Balaamu, akasema, "Ni nani watu hawa walio pamoja nawe?"
sw.B: Mungu alimjia Balaamu, akamwuliza, "Watu hawa wanaokaa kwako ni akina nani?"
sw.R: Usiku ule Mungu alimjia Balaamu. Akamwuliza, "Watu hawa walio pamoja nawe ni nani?"

decisions.choice: who are these men: a question that calls Balaam to account
decisions.reason: God does not ask because he does not know. As with Adam and Cain (Genesis 3:9; 4:9), the question makes Balaam say plainly what he is being asked to do.

decisions.choice: God: the narrator's word when God comes to Balaam
decisions.reason: In this chapter the narrator says "God" (Elohim) when God comes to Balaam (verses 9, 12, 20, 22), while Balaam speaks of "the LORD" (YHWH, verses 8, 13, 18-19), and the LORD acts in the story of the donkey (verses 22-35). Both name the one God of Israel.

decisions.choice: That night
decisions.reason: Readable says when God came, as verse 8 implies.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בִּלְעָ֖ם אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּלָ֧ק בֶּן־צִפֹּ֛ר מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָ֖ב שָׁלַ֥ח אֵלָֽי׃

en.L: And Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent [word] to me,
en.B: Balaam answered God, "Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, has sent me this message,
en.R: Balaam answered God, "Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, has sent me a message.

es.L: Y dijo Balaam a Dios: «Balac hijo de Zipor, rey de Moab, me ha enviado [un mensaje]:
es.B: Balaam respondió a Dios: «Balac hijo de Zipor, el rey de Moab, me ha enviado este mensaje:
es.R: Balaam le respondió a Dios: «Balac hijo de Zipor, el rey de Moab, me ha enviado un mensaje.

fr.L: Et Balaam dit à Dieu : « Balak fils de Tsippor, roi de Moab, m’a envoyé [un message] :
fr.B: Balaam répondit à Dieu : « Balak, fils de Tsippor, le roi de Moab, m’a envoyé ce message :
fr.R: Balaam a répondu à Dieu : « Balak, fils de Tsippor, le roi de Moab, m’a envoyé un message.

sw.L: Naye Balaamu akamwambia Mungu, "Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, amenitumia [ujumbe],
sw.B: Balaamu alimjibu Mungu, "Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, amenitumia ujumbe huu:
sw.R: Balaamu alimjibu Mungu, "Balaki mwana wa Sipori, mfalme wa Moabu, amenitumia ujumbe.

decisions.choice: has sent to me: the message follows
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; Balaam goes straight on to quote Balak's message in verse 11.

decisions.choice: [word] (L), this message (B), a message (R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "sent"; the levels supply what the next verse shows was sent.

source.text: הִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣א מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַיְכַ֖ס אֶת־עֵ֣ין הָאָ֑רֶץ עַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֤ה קָֽבָה־לִּי֙ אֹת֔וֹ אוּלַ֥י אוּכַ֛ל לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּ֖וֹ וְגֵרַשְׁתִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, the people that came out from Egypt, and it covers the eye of the land; now come, curse for me it; perhaps I will be able to fight against it and I will drive it out.

en.L: 'Look, the people that has come out of Egypt, it has covered the eye of the land. Now come, put a curse on it for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against it and drive it out.'"
en.B: 'The people that came out of Egypt are covering the face of the land. Come now and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"
en.R: He says, 'A nation has come out of Egypt, and they cover the land. Come now and curse them for me. Then perhaps I will be able to fight them and drive them away.'"

es.L: “Mira, el pueblo que ha salido de Egipto ha cubierto el ojo de la tierra. Ahora ven, échale una maldición por mí. Quizá podré pelear contra él y echarlo”».
es.B: “El pueblo que salió de Egipto está cubriendo la faz de la tierra. Ven ahora y échale una maldición por mí. Quizá así podré pelear contra él y expulsarlo”».
es.R: Dice: “Ha salido de Egipto una nación, y cubren la tierra. Ven ahora y maldícelos por mí. Así tal vez podré pelear contra ellos y echarlos”».

fr.L: “Voici, le peuple qui est sorti d’Égypte, il a couvert l’œil du pays. Maintenant viens, lance contre lui une malédiction pour moi. Peut-être pourrai-je combattre contre lui et le chasser.” »
fr.B: “Le peuple qui est sorti d’Égypte recouvre la surface du pays. Viens maintenant lancer une malédiction contre lui pour moi. Peut-être pourrai-je alors le combattre et le chasser.” »
fr.R: Il dit : “Un peuple est sorti d’Égypte, et ils couvrent le pays. Viens maintenant les maudire pour moi. Alors je pourrai peut-être les combattre et les chasser.” »

sw.L: 'Tazama, watu waliotoka Misri, wamefunika jicho la nchi. Basi sasa njoo, uwaapize kwa ajili yangu. Huenda nitaweza kupigana nao na kuwafukuza.'"
sw.B: 'Watu waliotoka Misri wameenea juu ya uso wa nchi. Njoo sasa uwaapize kwa ajili yangu. Huenda hapo nitaweza kupigana nao na kuwafukuza.'"
sw.R: Anasema, 'Taifa limetoka Misri, nao wamejaa katika nchi. Njoo sasa uwalaani kwa ajili yangu. Kisha huenda nitaweza kupigana nao na kuwafukuza.'"

decisions.choice: put a curse on: a second word for cursing
decisions.reason: Balak's message in verse 6 used the common word for "curse" ('arar). Balaam, repeating it, uses another word (qabab) that also means to curse, perhaps by naming someone for ruin. It comes again in verse 17 and in 23:8, where Balaam asks how he can curse one whom God has not cursed.

decisions.choice: fight against it: Balaam retells the message in his own words
decisions.reason: Balaam leaves out "it is dwelling opposite me" and "whoever you bless is blessed" (verses 5-6), and says "fight against" where Balak said "strike". What Balak asks for is the same.

decisions.choice: put a curse on (L, B), curse (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use a different English phrase for the second Hebrew word, so the reader can see the change (see m1); Readable says "curse" for both.

decisions.choice: "echar una maldición" for the second word for cursing (qabab); "maldecir" for 'arar
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the two Hebrew words apart, as the English does (see m1); Readable says "maldecir" for both.

decisions.choice: "lancer une malédiction contre" for the second word for cursing (qabab); "maudire" for 'arar
decisions.reason: As the English does with "put a curse on", Literal and Balanced keep the two Hebrew words apart (see m1); Readable says "maudire" for both. The same wording returns in verse 17 and in 23:8.

decisions.choice: "kuapiza" for the second word for cursing (qabab); "kulaani" for 'arar
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the two Hebrew words apart, as the English does (see m1); "kuapiza" is to call down harm on someone. Readable says "kulaani" for both.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־בִּלְעָ֔ם לֹ֥א תֵלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּהֶ֑ם לֹ֤א תָאֹר֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בָר֖וּךְ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Balaam, not you will go with them; not you will curse the people, for blessed [is] it.

en.L: And God said to Balaam, "You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for it [is] blessed."
en.B: But God said to Balaam, "You are not to go with them, nor are you to curse the people, because they are blessed."
en.R: But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with these men. Do not curse the people of Israel, because I have blessed them."

es.L: Y dijo Dios a Balaam: «No irás con ellos. No maldecirás al pueblo, porque [es] bendito».
es.B: Pero Dios dijo a Balaam: «No vayas con ellos, ni maldigas a ese pueblo, porque es bendito».
es.R: Pero Dios le dijo a Balaam: «No vayas con esos hombres. No maldigas al pueblo de Israel, porque yo lo he bendecido».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit à Balaam : « Tu n’iras pas avec eux. Tu ne maudiras pas le peuple, car il [est] béni. »
fr.B: Mais Dieu dit à Balaam : « Tu n’iras pas avec eux, et tu ne maudiras pas ce peuple, car il est béni. »
fr.R: Mais Dieu a dit à Balaam : « Ne pars pas avec ces hommes. Ne maudis pas le peuple d’Israël, car je l’ai béni. »

sw.L: Naye Mungu akamwambia Balaamu, "Hutakwenda pamoja nao. Hutawalaani watu hao, kwa maana wamebarikiwa."
sw.B: Lakini Mungu alimwambia Balaamu, "Usiende pamoja nao, wala usiwalaani watu hao, kwa sababu wamebarikiwa."
sw.R: Lakini Mungu alimwambia Balaamu, "Usiende pamoja na watu hawa. Usiwalaani Waisraeli, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nimewabariki."

decisions.choice: for it is blessed: Israel already stands under God's blessing
decisions.reason: God's answer is short and final. Israel is the people of the promise to Abraham (Genesis 12:2-3), and no seer's curse can undo what God has blessed (23:8, 20).

decisions.choice: You shall not: a firm prohibition
decisions.reason: "Not" with the plain future form states a firm rule, as in the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:13-15), not advice for one night.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel; I have blessed them
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and says who blessed them, since the blessing comes from God himself (Genesis 12:2; Numbers 23:20).

source.text: וַיָּ֤קָם בִּלְעָם֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־שָׂרֵ֣י בָלָ֔ק לְכ֖וּ אֶֽל־אַרְצְכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י מֵאֵ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה לְתִתִּ֖י לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Balaam in the morning and said to [the] princes of Balak, go to your land, for has refused YHWH to let me go with you.

en.L: And Balaam rose in the morning and said to the princes of Balak, "Go to your land, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has refused to let me go with you."
en.B: In the morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's officials, "Go back to your own country. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not allow me to go with you."
en.R: The next morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's leaders, "Go back home. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not let me go with you."

es.L: Y se levantó Balaam por la mañana y dijo a los príncipes de Balac: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se ha negado a dejarme ir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.B: Por la mañana Balaam se levantó y dijo a los dignatarios de Balac: «{{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} país. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no me permite ir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, Balaam se levantó y les dijo a los jefes de Balac: «{{plural_you:Regresen|Regresad}} a casa. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no me deja ir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».

fr.L: Et Balaam se leva le matin et dit aux princes de Balak : « Allez dans votre pays, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a refusé de me laisser aller avec vous. »
fr.B: Le matin, Balaam se leva et dit aux dignitaires de Balak : « Retournez dans votre pays. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne me permet pas d’aller avec vous. »
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, Balaam s’est levé et a dit aux chefs envoyés par Balak : « Rentrez chez vous. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne veut pas que j’aille avec vous. »

sw.L: Naye Balaamu akaamka asubuhi, akawaambia wakuu wa Balaki, "Nendeni katika nchi yenu, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekataa kuniacha niende pamoja nanyi."
sw.B: Asubuhi Balaamu aliamka, akawaambia maafisa wa Balaki, "Rudini katika nchi yenu. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hataniruhusu kwenda pamoja nanyi."
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi Balaamu aliamka, akawaambia viongozi wa Balaki, "Rudini nyumbani. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hataki niende pamoja nanyi."

decisions.choice: the LORD has refused to let me go: Balaam tells only half of God's answer
decisions.reason: God said both "you shall not go" and "you shall not curse, for they are blessed" (verse 12). Balaam tells the envoys only that he may not go and says nothing of the blessing. That leaves room for Balak to try again with a larger offer (verses 15-17).

decisions.choice: Go back home
decisions.reason: "Go to your land" means returning home; Readable says it simply.

records.literal_gloss: And arose [the] princes of Moab and came to Balak and said, refuses Balaam to come with us.

en.L: And the princes of Moab rose and came to Balak and said, "Balaam refuses to come with us."
en.B: So the officials of Moab set off, went back to Balak, and told him, "Balaam will not come with us."
en.R: So the leaders from Moab went back to Balak. They told him, "Balaam would not come with us."

es.L: Y se levantaron los príncipes de Moab, y vinieron a Balac y dijeron: «Balaam se niega a venir con nosotros».
es.B: Así que los dignatarios de Moab se pusieron en camino, volvieron a Balac y le dijeron: «Balaam no quiere venir con nosotros».
es.R: Entonces los jefes de Moab volvieron adonde estaba Balac. Le dijeron: «Balaam no quiso venir con nosotros».

fr.L: Et les princes de Moab se levèrent, vinrent vers Balak et dirent : « Balaam refuse de venir avec nous. »
fr.B: Les dignitaires de Moab partirent donc, retournèrent auprès de Balak et lui dirent : « Balaam ne veut pas venir avec nous. »
fr.R: Alors les chefs de Moab sont retournés chez Balak. Ils lui ont dit : « Balaam n’a pas voulu venir avec nous. »

sw.L: Nao wakuu wa Moabu wakaondoka, wakafika kwa Balaki, wakasema, "Balaamu anakataa kuja pamoja nasi."
sw.B: Basi maafisa wa Moabu waliondoka, wakarudi kwa Balaki, wakamwambia, "Balaamu hataki kuja pamoja nasi."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo viongozi wa Moabu walirudi kwa Balaki. Wakamwambia, "Balaamu amekataa kuja pamoja nasi."

decisions.choice: Balaam refuses: the envoys do not say why
decisions.reason: Balaam said it was the LORD who refused (verse 13); the envoys report only that Balaam refused. So Balak thinks the problem is the price, and he raises it (verses 15-17).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥סֶף ע֖וֹד בָּלָ֑ק שְׁלֹ֣חַ שָׂרִ֔ים רַבִּ֥ים וְנִכְבָּדִ֖ים מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And again yet Balak sent princes, many and honored more than these.

en.L: And Balak again sent princes, more numerous and more honored than these.
en.B: Balak sent officials once more, more of them than before, and of higher rank than the first.
en.R: Then Balak sent other leaders. This time there were more of them, and they were more important than the first ones.

es.L: Y volvió Balac a enviar príncipes, más numerosos y más honorables que aquellos.
es.B: Balac envió dignatarios una vez más, en mayor número que antes y de más alto rango que los primeros.
es.R: Entonces Balac envió a otros jefes. Esta vez eran más, y eran más importantes que los primeros.

fr.L: Et Balak envoya encore des princes, plus nombreux et plus honorés que ceux-là.
fr.B: Balak envoya de nouveau des dignitaires, plus nombreux que les premiers et d’un rang plus élevé.
fr.R: Alors Balak a envoyé d’autres chefs. Cette fois, ils étaient plus nombreux, et c’étaient des hommes plus importants que les premiers.

sw.L: Naye Balaki akatuma tena wakuu, wengi zaidi na wenye heshima zaidi kuliko hao.
sw.B: Balaki alituma maafisa mara nyingine, wengi kuliko wale wa kwanza na wenye vyeo vya juu zaidi.
sw.R: Kisha Balaki alituma viongozi wengine. Safari hii walikuwa wengi zaidi, na walikuwa watu wakubwa kuliko wale wa kwanza.

decisions.choice: more numerous and more honored: a greater embassy
decisions.reason: Sending more envoys, and men of higher rank, did Balaam greater honor and promised a greater reward (verse 17).

decisions.choice: again sent: literally "added again to send"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "add" with another verb to say an action is repeated. The same verb returns in the donkey story, where Balaam strikes her "again" (verse 25) and the angel moves on "again" (verse 26).

fr.B: Ils vinrent trouver Balaam et lui dirent : « Voici ce que dit Balak, fils de Tsippor : “Je t’en prie, que rien ne t’empêche de venir auprès de moi,

sw.R: Walifika kwa Balaamu, wakamwambia, "Balaki mwana wa Sipori anasema, 'Tafadhali, usiruhusu jambo lolote likuzuie kuja kwangu.

decisions.choice: Thus says: the words of a messenger
decisions.reason: Envoys spoke a king's words as if he were speaking, introduced by "thus says". The prophets use the same words for the message of the LORD.

decisions.choice: do not be held back: let nothing stop you
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: "do not let yourself be held back". Balak hints that something is keeping Balaam from coming and asks him not to give way to it.

decisions.choice: [anything]
decisions.reason: English needs a subject for "hold back"; Literal adds it in brackets.

source.text: כִּֽי־כַבֵּ֤ד אֲכַבֶּדְךָ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה וּלְכָה־נָּא֙ קָֽבָה־לִּ֔י אֵ֖ת הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

en.R: I will reward you richly. I will do anything you ask. So please come and curse these people for me.'"

fr.B: car je te comblerai d’honneurs et je ferai tout ce que tu me demanderas. Viens, je t’en prie, et lance pour moi une malédiction contre ce peuple.” »
fr.R: Je te récompenserai largement. Je ferai tout ce que tu me demanderas. Alors, s’il te plaît, viens maudire ce peuple pour moi.” »

sw.B: kwa maana nitakupa heshima kubwa na kufanya lolote utakaloniomba. Njoo, tafadhali, uwaapize watu hawa kwa ajili yangu.'"
sw.R: Nitakupa zawadi nyingi sana. Nitafanya lolote utakaloniomba. Basi tafadhali njoo uwalaani watu hawa kwa ajili yangu.'"

decisions.choice: honor: reward with wealth and high standing
decisions.reason: To "honor" someone here means to give him rich gifts and rank. Balaam hears it as silver and gold (verse 18), and Balak uses the word again in verse 37 and 24:11.

decisions.choice: I will greatly honor you: an emphatic promise
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled ("honoring I will honor") and "greatly" is added, to press the offer as hard as Balak can.

decisions.choice: put a curse on: the second word for cursing
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: reward you richly
decisions.reason: Readable says what the honor would be (see m1).
